question: A library has a million books. Why does its catalog, sorted by title, make finding one book fast?
options: It lets you skip straight to the right drawer and card instead of walking every shelf
It makes the shelves themselves shorter
It keeps a copy of every book in the drawers
It sorts the books on the shelves every night
explanation: The catalog is an index: a small sorted structure that points to where each book is. Each label narrows the search, so a few steps replace a walk past a million books. It does not move or copy the books, and it must be updated when a book arrives.
